phase3_findings.description: _CatalogCursor.execute answers every parameterless statement with (lower_case_table_names,), so the runner's SELECT @@SESSION.sql_mode probe (run when remove_sql_modes is set) would read 0 and send SET SESSION sql_mode = '0' with no error; no current test reaches it, but a future rule-set test on FakeMySQL would pass with a wrong session setup.

Changed comments in test_tool_dialect_alone_decides_the_output say the statement 'does not parse, so it is not read-shaped', but is_read_shaped only checks the first token via first_sql_keyword and never parses; the new mysql row uses different SQL text, so the dialect alone does not decide it as the test name says.

test_hash_is_not_a_comment_outside_mysql gained a mysql row ('x\nSHOW ...') that has no '#', but the unchanged body comment still explains the outcome by '#' opening a comment only in MySQL; that reason fits only the sqlite row, and the test name has the same drift.

The fake's module docstring says a parameterless statement gets the @@lower_case_table_names answer without noting the sql_mode probe gets the same; line 145 says kinds is keyed by the relation name 'as written in the SQL' while the lookup uses the parsed identifier without backticks.

In test_mysql_alias_hides_secret_but_unaliased_expression_is_masked, the assertion expression.columns.tolist() == ['upper(password_hash)'] checks a label the test scripted into server.rows, so it cannot fail because of the runner or masking guard; the masking assertions and the live connector test carry the real checks.
